9.0.s.en: 1. God sets man up as lord

9.0.0.en: 1 O God of the fathers, O Lord of mercy, who hast made all things by thy word, 2 and formed man by thy wisdom, that he should have dominion over the creatures which thou hast made, 3 and rule the world in holiness and righteousness, and execute judgment with an upright soul.

9.0.1.en: "O God of my fathers, and Lord of mercy, who hast made all things by thy word. [1]

9.0.2.en: At the beginning of his reign Solomon turns his face toward God to ask Him for the enjoyment of wisdom. Here he calls upon God with the following titles:

9.1.0.en: By the fathers he means the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and perhaps he also had in mind Noah and Moses the prophet and Joshua the son of Nun and some of the judges and King David and others. All of them were great leaders, each with his distinct personality, yet each one completes the others, for God is the supreme Leader of leaders.

9.1.1.en: He calls the leaders fathers, and God attributes Himself to the fathers: "God of the fathers." For leadership in the mind of Solomon the wise is nothing but fatherhood and tenderness and gentleness toward others, so that all become for him as those in the place of sons. He exercises leadership not from a position of authority with commands and prohibitions, but from the position of fatherhood!

9.1.2.en: If the Creator of heaven and earth presents Himself to His creation as the God of the fathers, how much more does it befit civil and religious leaders to open their hearts to others with a kind of fatherhood.

9.1.3.en: Leadership is not merely a position in the Church or the administration of certain works or merely rituals and duties carried out in any manner, but it is first and before everything fatherhood, which the servant receives as a gift from the Lord who called him.

9.1.4.en: And God, in offering fatherhood to His children the servants, offers them its essence and its pillar, love, without which we cannot taste the truth of fatherhood or feel its presence. He also trains His children and develops them in the school of love from childhood, that they may be like God, and not be harsh fathers who provoke their children and destroy them. For this reason we say that the only school from which the true servants of God graduate in the Old and New Testaments, which still is and will remain so until the faithful men of God graduate in it, is the school of Christian love.

9.1.5.en: * O teacher, intercessor of the divine mysteries, speak with love.

9.1.6.en: He who teaches and does not love is restrained by silence, for in vain he wearies himself composing unprofitable words.

9.1.7.en: The great master, if he wishes to win his hearers, let him love much and speak little with his disciples.

9.1.8.en: St. Jacob of Serugh. * I teach that the man who is placed over the community and rules over them is not supported and magnified by anything like showing deep love for those under him.

9.1.9.en: For a father is not a father merely because he begot sons but because he loves them. So if nature requires this love of necessity, how much more the sonship that is by grace? I mean, if a person must love his natural children in order to be called a natural father, how much more must he love his children according to grace, the spiritual ones who are baptized, lest they become punished in Gehenna.

9.1.10.en: St. John Chrysostom. * His coming (Christ's) has poured out upon mankind a great gift of fatherly grace.

9.1.11.en: St. Irenaeus. * How great is God's love for men! For He granted to those who had departed from Him and fallen into the abyss of vices the forgiveness of sins and an abundant share of grace, so that they call Him Father, saying: "Our Father which art in heaven." The heavens are those who bear the image of the heavenly world, and in whom God dwells and abides.

9.2.0.en: Since Solomon is speaking with God, asking Him for the wisdom that gives him the spirit of fatherhood toward his people, and indeed toward every man, he calls God "Lord of mercy." For man cannot enjoy the spirit of tenderness and kindness and gentleness toward others unless the merciful God gives him this gift.

9.2.1.en: For mercy in its essence is not a passing emotion toward a suffering or needy person, but is a sharing in a characteristic particular to God, who is true "Love," the giver of mercy as an inward trait in the soul, so that man has mercy even on those who oppose him, as he has mercy on animals, and is gentle with everything.

9.2.2.en: * "Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy"... He gave mercy to the merciful because they accept true and wonderful counsel, so that the One greater than they (God) deals with them in the same way in which they deal with those lesser than themselves: "Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy."

9.2.3.en: St. Augustine. * Let us be merciful, as it is written, so that God may be merciful to us (Mt 5:7).

9.2.4.en: * Moses led the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, and was chosen from tending sheep to tend his people, and he led them as a good shepherd. Moses carried his rod on his shoulder, and went before his people whom he led, and shepherded them forty years, and he was watchful and toiled for his flock; he was a good shepherd. When his Lord wished to destroy them because of their sins, when they worshiped the calf, Moses prayed for them and asked his Lord, saying: "Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written" (Ex 32:32). This is the exceedingly watchful shepherd, who gives himself up for his flock. This is the excellent leader who lays down himself for his flock. This is the merciful father who embraces his sons and brings them up.

9.3.s.en: C. Creator of all by His word:

9.3.0.en: Solomon directs his prayer to God, the Creator of all by His word or wisdom. It is not enough for the leader to be a merciful father, but he must imitate God the Creator who brought all things into being by His word, who is the wisdom of God. So the leader is to be prudent and wise.

9.3.1.en: For some do wrong even with regard to their own children, offering tenderness and burning emotion without prudence and without discernment and wisdom. For this reason Father Gregory (the Great) tells us that pastoral care or leadership is an art.

9.3.2.en: * It is true medicine when we treat a sickness that is in the body and at the same time heal the prevailing needs of the body. If the medicine of the body can be compounded and prescribed to serve different ends, is it not even more fitting for the medicine of the soul, which comes in the folds of one teaching and which is the art of the lofty arts, treating things that are not seen, to conquer the various moral evils?

9.3.3.en: * Treatment at the wrong time makes wounds more painful. And if the medicines are not suitable, they are certainly not fit for the purpose of healing.

9.3.4.en: * The shepherd of souls must discern with wisdom and care between virtues and vices, lest stinginess take hold of his heart while he exaggerates in appearing as a good manager, or lest he boast of his generosity as though it were a virtue when in truth he is a spendthrift and a destroyer. Or lest he overlook what he ought to criticize sharply, and so bring eternal punishment upon his flock, or punish faults without mercy, and so sin a greater sin, or when he spoils what he could have done with dignity and uprightness by his hasty and rash expectations. Likewise the postponing of a good deed may turn it into an evil deed.

9.4.0.en: And formed man by thy wisdom, that he should have dominion over the creatures which thou hast made. [2]

9.5.s.en: D. The divine Leader who raises up leaders, not slaves

9.5.0.en: The wise man stands in amazement before the wisdom of the Creator, which is manifested not only in creating man with this surpassing creativity, nor in His care for him in that He created the world for his sake, but, what is greater, in the wisdom He gave him to rule the earthly creation. It is marvelous that the Creator gives man this authority, and offers him wisdom, to raise him up as a leader to rule over the world. For God said to Adam, charging him and his wife and their descendants after them: "Have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed" (Gen 1:29).

9.6.0.en: And rule the world in holiness and righteousness, and execute judgment with an upright soul. [3]

9.6.1.en: E. The Holy and Righteous One raises up righteous saints who rule with justice and not with injustice. If God by His wisdom made man wise, knowing how to rule over creation, then, being the Holy and Righteous One without sin, He granted man to be holy and righteous so that he may rule the world in holiness and righteousness, and judge in all matters with an upright soul or an upright heart.

9.6.2.en: God set man up to be truly an icon of the Holy and Righteous One, and he himself becomes a temple of the Holy One without blemish, in which God dwells. Indeed he even desires to see all his brothers and sisters holy and righteous, so that each man and woman sees in everyone the dazzling image of God.

9.6.3.en: Thus nothing occupies the heart of the true believer like being holy and righteous in the Lord, and seeing all mankind become holy and righteous, blameless before God.

9.7.0.en: 4 Give me wisdom, that sitteth by thy throne; and reject me not from among thy children: 5 For I am thy servant and the son of thine handmaid, a feeble man and of a short time, and lacking in understanding of judgment and laws. 6 But if there be one perfect among the children of men, yet if thy wisdom be not with him, he shall be counted as nothing.

9.7.1.en: Give me wisdom, that sitteth with thee by thy throne, and cast me not off from among thy children. [4]

9.7.2.en: The wise man looked toward God, the giver of wisdom, and saw Him as:

9.7.3.en: · Father of the fathers, the giver of true fatherhood.

9.7.4.en: · Lord of mercy, the giver of tenderness and kindness.

9.7.5.en: · Creator by His word, and by His wisdom the giver of wisdom and discernment.

9.7.6.en: · The divine Leader, who raises up leaders and not slaves.

9.7.7.en: · The Holy One, who raises up saints as witnesses to Him, who rule with righteousness and holiness.

9.7.8.en: This is on God's side; what then is man's part, that he may enjoy the wisdom of God?

9.7.9.en: Here Solomon stands to see the wisdom of God, the Second Hypostasis seated on the throne, and who can reach Him? There is no way to cross over to Him, but by His humility He comes down to us, and in the spirit of humility we meet with Him to possess Him.

9.7.10.en: He is seated on the throne, but He is not far from us, for He takes the initiative with practical love, bows the heavens and comes down, to stand at the doors of our hearts asking to enter. He does not break into our hearts or our thoughts without our will, but waits for us to invite Him! For our part we realize that by His coming down He made us His sons, and opened for us the door of Baptism and paid the price by the Cross. We must ask Him in hope and boldness not to cast us off, for we are His sons.

9.7.11.en: He knocks at the doors of our hearts with His surpassing love and humility, and we knock at His doors with prayer in the spirit of humility, with hope and boldness!

9.7.12.en: If God created man to rule over creatures and to govern the world in holiness and righteousness, who can give him these resources but the wisdom that sits on the divine throne? She sets man up as a wise lord, able to act with power and wisdom, in holiness and righteousness. However great man's perfection and gifts and abilities and resources may be, without divine wisdom man is counted as nothing.

9.7.13.en: * Wisdom must be sought from God alone and not from philosophers or astrologers. God gives wisdom like a spring whose waters will not cease, and waters everyone who enters by it; but the wisdom of philosophers and other human agencies is not given generously, and soon dries up.

9.7.14.en: Hilary of Arles. * What blessing does that man not possess who seeks this wisdom and receives it from the Lord? This gives you understanding. What a grace this is; for if this wisdom were from ourselves it would not be from above, and we would not ask it from God who created us.

9.8.0.en: St. Augustine. For I am thy servant and the son of thine handmaid, a weak man and short-lived, with little understanding of judgment and laws. [5]

9.8.1.en: King Solomon confesses that he is a servant of the Lord and the son of His handmaid; what he receives from God is by His free grace and generous love, and not by personal merit. In the spirit of humility the king declares his inability to accomplish his mission with which God entrusted him, for his days are short and his understanding little, he has no knowledge nor learning nor experience, so he is in need of the grace of God, the giver of wisdom and understanding and insight.

9.8.2.en: * The weak in the flesh, who being wise in the world forsake their knowledge... become as children of their own free will, and so learn the wisdom that is not acquired by the toil of study.

9.8.3.en: St. Isaac the Syrian. * God grants wisdom that we may understand it as is fitting.

9.8.4.en: Theodoret, bishop of Cyrus. * Those who wish to return to their first rank will not be able to do so except by humility. For pride was the cause of the fall at the beginning from heaven. And so whoever lacks deep humility from all his heart and mind and spirit and body does not inherit the kingdom of God.

9.9.0.en: St. Anthony the Great. For though one be perfect among the children of men, yet if thy wisdom be not with him, he shall be counted as nothing. [6]

9.9.1.en: Solomon realized that the feeling of self-sufficiency and not hungering and thirsting for God deprives man of every divine spiritual gift, even if he appears in the eyes of men successful and good and perfect.

9.9.2.en: * Everything that a person has through natural creation, when he exercises it, he receives what is through the grace of God. Thus he has an abundance and comes to be in a stronger state in what he has. This is not only with regard to wisdom, but in every good thing we must reflect upon the words of Solomon: "For though a man be perfect among the children of men, and thy wisdom be not with him, he shall be counted as nothing.

9.9.3.en: Origen. * The man who is wise by the standards of the world is in truth very ignorant, because he does not put away corrupt teaching. A little learning is a dangerous thing, for it makes those who possess it unwilling to learn more. The unlearned are more ready to learn; they are not so ignorant as those who think themselves wise.

9.10.0.en: 7 Thou hast chosen me to be a king of thy people, and a judge of thy sons and daughters, 8 and hast commanded me to build a temple upon thy holy mount, and an altar in the city of thy dwelling, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle which thou hast prepared from the beginning.

9.10.1.en: Thou hast chosen me to be a king of thy people, and a judge of thy sons and daughters. [7]

9.10.2.en: Solomon prayed and received, for along with his realization of God's surpassing resources, and his need to enjoy God's wisdom and grace, he also realized that he has a special, distinct mission that will not be accomplished by human resources, but by the grace of God ready to work. For besides the general mission to which every man is committed, every person has a special mission, which it befits him to recognize in order to accomplish it according to God's plan and divine good pleasure. So Solomon was set up as king over the people of God for a mission according to God's plan.

9.11.0.en: And hast commanded me to build a temple upon thy holy mount, and an altar in thy dwelling place, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which thou hast prepared from the beginning. [8]

9.11.1.en: It was not possible for Moses the prophet to set up the tabernacle of the testimony according to his own human thought, but he set it up according to the pattern which the Lord showed him in heaven, that it might be an icon of heaven. For it is said: "Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount" (Heb 8:5).

9.11.2.en: And now it was not in Solomon's mind to build the holy temple identical to the tent of meeting, but according to the holy tabernacle which God had prepared from the beginning, that is, the one existing in heaven.

9.11.3.en: This is the mission of every true believer, to set up by the Holy Spirit of God and divine wisdom a temple for the Lord after the likeness of heaven itself. As Holy Scripture says:

9.11.4.en: "Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?" (1 Cor 3:16).

9.11.5.en: "If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are" (1 Cor 3:17).

9.11.6.en: "What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?" (1 Cor 6:19).

9.11.7.en: "Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God: and I will write upon him my new name" (Rev 3:12).

9.11.8.en: "He that sitteth on the throne shall dwell among them" (Rev 7:15).

9.11.9.en: * Everyone whom the Word of God leads to strive together in the way of godliness is a precious stone in the one great temple of God. Therefore Peter the Apostle says: "Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ" (1 Pet 2:5). And Paul the Apostle also says: "And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone" (Eph 2:20). Something similar is also found by a hidden allusion in that passage of Isaiah in which he addresses Jerusalem: "Behold, I will build thy stones with antimony, and lay thy foundations with sapphires, and make thy pinnacles rubies, and thy gates of carbuncle stones, and all thy borders of precious stones, and all thy children shall be taught of the Lord, and great shall be the peace of thy children" (Isa 54:11-14).

9.11.10.en: So among the righteous there are some who are antimony, and some who are sapphire, and others carbuncle, or precious stones, that is, there are in them all kinds for choosing.

9.12.0.en: 9 With thee is wisdom, which knoweth thy works, and which was present when thou madest the world, and knoweth what is pleasing in thine eyes, and what is right in thy commandments. 10 O send her out of thy holy heavens, and send her from the throne of thy glory, that being present she may labour with me, and I may know what is pleasing unto thee. 11 For she knoweth and understandeth all things, and she shall be to me a prudent guide in my doings, and preserve me by her glory. 12 So shall my works be acceptable, and I shall judge thy people with justice, and shall be worthy of my father's throne. 13 For what man is he that can know the counsel of God? or who can discern what the Lord willeth? 14 For the thoughts of men are hesitant, and our insights are not firm. 15 For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthly dwelling weigheth down the mind that is full of cares. 16 And hardly do we picture the things that are upon earth, and with toil do we perceive the things that are before us: but the things that are in the heavens, who hath searched them out?

9.12.1.en: With thee is wisdom, which knoweth thy works, and was present when thou madest the world, and knoweth what is pleasing in thine eyes, and what is right according to thy commandments. [9]

9.12.2.en: Solomon the wise looks toward the divine throne and sees the divine hypostasis of wisdom seated upon it, the object of the Father's delight and good pleasure. It is as though he had already heard the voice of the heavenly Father during the baptism of the Lord Christ as well as during His transfiguration: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (Mt 3:17; 17:5; Mk 1:11; Lk 3:22; 2 Pet 1:17).

9.12.3.en: Solomon realized man's inability to be an object of the Father's delight, after he chose disobedience of his own will, and in pride accepted the counsel of the devil instead of believing the divine promises.

9.12.4.en: Solomon longed to acquire the divine wisdom and to be hidden in Him, so that through Him he might become an object of the Father's delight, and Solomon himself also take delight in God.

9.12.5.en: Holy Scripture has expressed the mutual delight between God and man in Jesus Christ the Crucified, who offered reconciliation between the Father and man. For this reason it is often said of the burnt offering, the symbol of the Cross: "it is a burnt offering unto the LORD: it is a sweet savour, an offering made by fire unto the LORD" (Ex 29:18; cf. Ex 29:15, 41; Lev 1:9, 17, etc.). This is about God's delight in us in Christ, the object of His delight. As for our side, it is said: "The fear of the Lord is glory, and boasting, and gladness, and a crown of rejoicing" (Sir 1:11). "The service keeps the heart, and justifies it, and gives gladness and joy" (Sir 1:18).

9.12.6.en: This is what drove Solomon toward seeking wisdom, since through the hypostasis of wisdom he becomes an object of God's delight, and himself enjoys delight and joy. The son of Sirach says of wisdom: "Whoever loves her loves life, and they that seek to her early shall be filled with joy. He that holdeth her fast shall inherit glory, and wheresoever she entereth, there is the blessing of the Lord" (Sir 4:12-13).

9.12.7.en: * Make us happy, O my God, in our occupation with You, so that we do not lose You.

9.12.8.en: * I say, happy is he who possesses God.

9.13.0.en: St. Augustine. O send her out of thy holy heavens, and send her from the throne of thy glory, that being present she may stand by me and labour with me, and I may know what is pleasing unto thee. [10]

9.13.1.en: Solomon was longing for the coming of the Lord Christ, the heavenly Word. He asks that the wisdom of God come down from the holy heavens, to carry him to heaven and bestow upon him the holy life. And that He be sent from the throne of glory, to bring him in to the throne.

9.13.2.en: The wisdom of God came to stand at our side against the devil, and to work in us and by us and with us, and to disclose to us the Father's delight in us.

9.13.3.en: * James (Jas 1:6) shows that the foundation of all human wisdom is faith. Here he attacks Simon the Magician, who asked the two Apostles to give him the Holy Spirit, and did not ask to receive faith.

9.13.4.en: Hilary of Arles. * Today "the carpenter's son"... made for Himself a living ladder, setting its base upon the earth, and its head rose toward heaven, and upon it God rests.

9.13.5.en: It is she whose image Jacob contemplated (Gen 28:12); by her God came down in His steadfastness, or rather bowed down in condescension, and "shewed himself upon earth, and conversed with men" (Bar 3:38).

9.13.6.en: Father John of Damascus. * How does God take the wise in their own craftiness? (Job 5:13) By showing them, while they think they are able to work without God, that they rather have need of Him. They enter into distress until they show themselves to be less than fishermen and the unlearned, and where they cannot work without their wisdom.

9.14.0.en: St. John Chrysostom. For she knoweth and understandeth all things, and shall lead me wisely in my doings, and preserve me by her glory. [11]

9.14.1.en: Who knoweth the Father but the Son, and he to whom the Son reveals Him? The Son, "Wisdom," alone is able to disclose to us the divine mysteries, and to give us our understanding, and to take us by the hands to lead us to heavenly glory, keeping us from the evil enemy.

9.14.2.en: * Spiritual wisdom is the cause of every perfect work. This is the heavenly wisdom, and when we are strengthened by it we can do everything perfectly.

9.14.3.en: Theophylact. * It is right for us to be there in the presence of God in the heavens, we who kept the lesson while we were on earth, and went there to heaven to be in the love of God the Father, whom we knew while on earth, and because God the Word the Holy One made all things and taught us and teaches us all things, and He trains us in all good things.

9.15.0.en: St. Clement of Alexandria. So shall my works be acceptable, and I shall judge thy people righteously, and shall be worthy of my father's throne. [12]

9.15.1.en: Without the Lord Christ our works will not be accepted, nor will our mission be accomplished.

9.15.2.en: * Do you also concede this, that Christ is "the power of God, and the wisdom of God"? You answer: "We concede this."

9.15.3.en: Listen then: "The spirit of the righteous is the seat of wisdom" (Wis 1). Yes, for what is the seat of God but the place where He dwells? And where does God dwell but in His temple? "For the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are" (1 Cor 3:17).

9.15.4.en: Be watchful in your reception of God. "God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth" (Jn 4:24).

9.15.5.en: Let the ark of the covenant enter your hearts, and let Dagon fall, if you will" (1 Sam 5:3).

9.15.6.en: Listen now. And learn to long for God. Be ready to learn how to see God. For He says: "Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God."

9.16.0.en: St. Augustine. For what man is he that can know the counsel of God? or who can conceive what the will of the Lord is? [13]

9.16.1.en: Our Christ declares in us the divine will, and gives us the ability to carry it out in practice.

9.16.2.en: * If I am not mistaken, it is not mentioned anywhere that He (Jesus Christ) prayed with His disciples. In every place He prayed alone, because human prayers cannot take hold of the counsels of God (Wis 9:13; Isa 40:13), and no one can share in the inner mysteries of Christ.

9.17.0.en: St. Ambrose. For the thoughts of mortal men are miserable, and our considerations are not firm [14]

9.17.1.en: Solomon the wise confesses that he is in need of the divine wisdom, who declares the will of the Father and fulfills it in us, and even gives us steadfastness in Him, so that our thoughts are not like a storm at the mercy of the winds, nor our longings and thoughts wavering.

9.17.2.en: * The psalmist sings: "Come ye unto him, and be enlightened: and your faces shall not be ashamed" (Ps 34:5). We draw near to God by faith, and faith is the work of the spirit and not of the body. But since we do not know what degree of perfection the spiritual body attains, for we are speaking here of a matter in which we have no experience, but on the responsibility of Holy Scripture we do not speak in a definite manner, we must have recourse to the words of the Book of Wisdom: "The thoughts of men are hesitant, and our considerations are not firm" (Wis 9:14).

9.18.0.en: St. Augustine. For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthly tabernacle weigheth down the mind that is full of cares. [15]

9.18.1.en: Origen sees that those who love God with all their souls and desire to be united with Him draw themselves away from the weight of the (lusts of the) body and all material things, praying with the Apostle Paul: "O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death?" (Rom 7:24). They groan in this tabernacle (that of the body), being burdened with the corruptible body (2 Cor 5:4).

9.18.2.en: * Why then do we hesitate and doubt to put off the corruptible man who hinders us and weighs down the soul, the earthly tabernacle that fills the mind with many cares, so that we may be freed from our bonds, and turn back from the stormy waves that are the lot of flesh and blood? For by this we enjoy Christ Jesus, the rest that accompanies blessedness, and contemplate in Him in His fullness the life-giving Word. And as we feed on Him we perceive the manifold wisdom in Him, and are sealed with the very truth, and our minds are enlightened with the light of true knowledge that does not grow dim, and we enjoy the sight of those things which are seen by the eyes enlightened by the commandment of the Lord (Ps 19:8; Eph 1:18).

9.18.3.en: Origen. * We were told by the prophet to rend our hearts and not our garments (Joel 2:13), which we can do when we remember that we ourselves often sin at least in thought if not in deed. For the earthly tabernacle represents the mind full of cares (Wis 9:15), and our earth does not cease to produce thorns and thistles for us. We are unable to eat our bread unless we toil with effort and the sweat of our brow.

9.18.4.en: Father Fulgentius. * Even if our dust is to some extent bound to evil, and the earthly tabernacle presses down upon the soul that flies to the heights (Wis 9:15), which was created to soar on high; yet let the image be washed from defilement and lift up the body that is its partner in the yoke, lifting it up on the two wings of the mind.

9.18.5.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus. * We must not ascribe deviation in the wandering of the heart to human nature or to its Creator, for Holy Scripture says truly: "God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions" (Eccl 7:29). The difference of thoughts depends upon ourselves, for good thought draws near to those who know it and the sensible man finds it. So whatever is subject to our discernment and our work we can attain, and if we do not attain it this is due to our laziness and neglect and not to a fault in our nature.

9.18.6.en: If this matter were not within our power the Lord would not have rebuked the Pharisees, saying: "Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?" (Mt 9:4). Nor would the prophet have been commissioned to say: "put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes" (Isa 1:16), "How long shall thy vain thoughts lodge within thee?" (Jer 4:14), nor would the kind of our thoughts have been considered on the Day of Judgment, since God threatens through Isaiah, saying: "And I will recompense their works and their thoughts" (Isa 66:18). It would not be right to recompense or punish according to the testimony of our thoughts in that dreadful and deadly examination, since the blessed Apostle says: "their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another. In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men according to my gospel" (Rom 2:15-16).

9.18.7.en: Father Serenus. * Shall we be young or old when we rise? If we die young (as children) and rise young, we shall need nurses in the resurrection. In any case, if we die young and rise old, then the dead do not rise at all; they will be changed into new beings.

9.18.8.en: Will there be distinction of sex in the world to come? Or will there be no such distinction? If the distinction continues there will be marriage and bodily relations and the begetting of children. If it does not continue, then the bodies that will rise will not be themselves. It is said: "The earthly tabernacle weigheth down the mind that is full of cares" (Wis 9:15). But the bodies that we have in heaven will be refined and spiritual, as the Apostle says: "It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body" (1 Cor 15:44).

9.18.9.en: St. Jerome. * Share with me in my labor, for you see what I have undertaken, and who I am who have undertaken it. You see what I desire to speak about, and where and what my condition is except that I am in [the corruptible body that weighs down the soul, and the earthly dwelling that weighs down the mind full of many cares (cf. Wis 9:15). Therefore I strip my thought of the many things, and gather it in the one God, the indivisible Trinity, so that I may be able to see something to speak about. Let them know that in that [body (which) weighs down the soul] I am able to say "Unto thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul" (Ps 25:1) LXX (that I may be able to speak to you of things worthy of the subject). May the Lord help me and lift up my soul with me. For I am very weak in relation to Him, and He is very mighty in relation to me."

9.18.10.en: * (The righteous) who have died have truly been stripped of the corruptible body that weighs down the soul (Wis 9:15). But they still await the redemption of their bodies (Rom 8:23), where their bodies rest in hope (Acts 2:26), but have not yet shone with the incorruption that is to come.

9.18.11.en: * Let us bear in mind that in this body that weighs down the soul (Wis 9:15) we live a miserable life.

9.18.12.en: * We are men who carry a body, which walks in this life; and although we have been born again of the seed of the word of God, yet in Christ we have been renewed in such a way that we have still not been completely delivered from Adam. For truly the mortal and corruptible part weighs down the soul (Wis 9:15), showing itself to be present, and declaring that it is from Adam, but what is spiritual in us and raises up the soul is the gift of God and of His mercy, who sent His only-begotten Son to share our death and lead us to His immortality.

9.18.13.en: * Let us lift up our souls to God, and not against God, for it is said: "Unto thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul" (Ps 25:1). Let us lift them up with His help, for they are heavy. And what is the cause of their heaviness? Because the corruptible body weighs down the soul (Wis 9:15), and the earthly tabernacle presses upon it, and it is occupied with many things.

9.18.14.en: * Since we are burdened with such a very heavy load, under which we groan, how shall I lift up my soul unless He lifts it up with me, He who gave Himself for me?

9.18.15.en: * On one side our corruptible body is a weight upon our souls, and on the other the cause of this hindrance is not in the nature and essence of the body. Therefore, since we know its corruption, we do not desire to be unclothed of the body but rather that it put on its incorruption. In the immortal life we shall have a body, but it will no longer be a weight since it will no longer be corruptible... We have been weighed down, then, by this corruptible body. But since we know that this state of weight is not from the nature and essence of the body but from its corruption, we therefore do not desire to be rid of it but to put it on with its incorruption. Then there will be a body, but it will no longer be a weight because it will no longer be corruptible.

9.18.16.en: * This body that is dead because of sin lives, which is without doubt corruptible and is a weight upon the soul (Wis 9:13).

9.18.17.en: * The word "corruptible" was added to show that the soul is weighed down not by any body whatever, but by the body that has come to this state through the fruit of sin.

9.18.18.en: * If every sin is evil, who can resist? We answer: The nature of man is good and at the same time also able to be freed from evil. For this reason we pray earnestly: "deliver us from evil" (Mt 6:13). This deliverance is not fully accomplished as long as the soul is weighed down by the body that hastens toward corruption (Wis 9:15). In any case, this process is accomplished by grace through faith, so that it is said: [O death, where is thy struggle? O death, where is thy sting? The sting of death is sin; and the strength of sin is the law] (cf. 1 Cor 15:55-56).

9.18.19.en: * The prayer of the whole City of God, while she is in a state of exile, cries out to God with the mouth of all her members: "Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors" (Mt 6:12). This prayer is effective not for those who have a dead faith without works (Jas 2:17), but for those whose faith worketh by love (Gal 5:6). For they, though subject to God, are weighed down by the corruptible body (Wis 9:15), so long as it is mortal, and it has not complete authority over vice. For this reason the righteous need this prayer. For although they exercise authority, the vices do not submit without resistance.

9.18.20.en: St. Augustine. St. Augustine fears that the believer may fall into despair when he is fought with a fleshly lust or a carnal thought that weighs upon the soul, for as long as man is in this world the corruptible body remains resisting, but there is a great difference between resistance and surrender.

9.18.21.en: * Although every crime is a sin, not every sin is a crime. Thus we say that the life of the saints may be free from crime, but as John the Apostle says: "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us" (1 Jn 1:8). But even crimes themselves, however great, can be forgiven in the Holy Church, and there is no despair of God's mercy for those who truly repent, each according to the measure of his sin.

9.19.0.en: St. Augustine. And hardly do we guess at things that are upon earth, and with difficulty do we find the things that are before us: but the things that are in the heavens, who can discover? [16]

9.19.1.en: With difficulty man can come to know some of the secrets of the visible world, and yet he still stands on the shore of the ocean of knowledge, so how can he come to know the secrets of the heavenly God and the heavenly things? Does he not need the divine wisdom to declare by Himself concerning Himself and His Father and His Holy Spirit?

9.19.2.en: * While the seraphim are not able even to behold God, who does not reveal Himself to them except as a condescension on His part according to their weakness, we see men who dare to picture in their minds the very nature which the seraphim are unable to comprehend. They claim that they are able to look upon it clearly and without limits. Tremble, O heavens, and be astonished, O earth".

9.19.3.en: * "Truly God is incomprehensible and cannot be approached, even for these orders. For this reason He condescends to appear in the manner recorded in the Revelation. God, who is not bounded by place and does not sit upon a throne... out of His love for us appears seated on a throne with the heavenly powers surrounding Him.

9.19.4.en: When He appeared on the throne and these powers surrounded Him, these powers could not behold Him nor bear to look at the brightness of His light, so they covered their eyes with their wings, and they had nothing left but to praise and sing with hymns full of glory and holy trembling, and songs bearing witness to the holiness of Him who sits upon the throne."

9.20.0.en: 17 And thy counsel who hath known, except thou give wisdom, and send thy Holy Spirit from above? 18 For so the ways of them which are upon the earth were set straight, and men were taught the things that are pleasing unto thee, 19 and by wisdom were saved all that pleased thee, O Lord, from the beginning.

9.20.1.en: And who hath known thy counsel, except thou give wisdom, and send thy Holy Spirit from on high? [17]

9.20.2.en: Our Christ, who loved us even unto death so as to save us and bring us into union with Him, offers us on the night of His passion another Comforter, saying:

9.20.3.en: "But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you" (Jn 14:16-18, 26).

9.20.4.en: "But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, he shall testify of me" (Jn 15:26).

9.20.5.en: "Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come. He shall glorify me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you" (Jn 16:13-14).

9.20.6.en: * A man does not have wisdom and understanding and counsel and fortitude and knowledge and godliness and the fear of God unless he receives the spirit of wisdom and understanding and counsel and fortitude and knowledge and godliness and the fear of God, according to the saying of the Apostle (2 Tim 1:7; Isa 11:2-3).

9.20.7.en: * This is the wisdom that tames the tongue, descending from above (Jas 3:17), and does not spring from a human heart. Would anyone dare to snatch it away from the grace of God and, in the conceit of pride, put it under the authority of man?

9.20.8.en: St. Augustine. * Wisdom is given not through a book that one learns, but through the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit.

9.20.9.en: Father Ambrosiaster. * When the soul is united with the Comforter Spirit in ineffable intimacy, and is wholly mingled with the Spirit, it is counted worthy to become itself spirit, and in its mingling with Him it then becomes wholly light and eye and joy and rest and gladness and love and compassion and goodness and tender mercies.

9.21.0.en: St. Macarius the Great. So the ways of them which live upon the earth were set straight, and men were taught what pleaseth thee, and by wisdom they received salvation." [18]

9.21.1.en: We were in need of the incarnation of God, the Son the Word, the Second Hypostasis, that the incarnate God might come forward, in the depths of His love for me, bearing death for me in His body. And though the mind is unable to comprehend the depths of God's love for him... God the Word becomes flesh, He who fills all with His divinity!! God the Word becomes incarnate to suffer and bear shame!!

9.21.2.en: * If they had given thanks to God who gave this wisdom, they would not have ascribed anything to themselves. For this reason the Lord gave them up to the lusts of their hearts and they did what is not fitting.

9.21.3.en: St. Augustine. * "We have peace with God" (Rom 5:1), through our Lord Jesus Christ who reconciled us with God through the sacrifice of His blood... Christ came to destroy the enemies, and to make peace, and to reconcile us with God from whom we had been separated by the barrier of evil that we set up by our sins.

9.21.5.en: Let me acquire You, O You who sit upon the throne

9.21.6.en: * I cry out to You, O Father of the fathers.

9.21.7.en: You want to make of me a father who loves all mankind.

9.21.8.en: You want to pour Your mercy into me, that I may become merciful through You, O Lord of mercy.

9.21.9.en: You wish to give me wisdom and understanding, O my Creator!

9.21.10.en: * You created me to rule the world in holiness and righteousness.

9.21.11.en: Sanctify me and I shall be sanctified, and I shall long to see the whole world sanctified to You.

9.21.12.en: Justify me and I shall be justified, and I shall not cease from prayer and constant work, until all are justified by You.

9.21.13.en: You did not create man a slave but free.

9.21.14.en: You created him that his heart might open with love to all mankind.

9.21.15.en: He rules, not by domination nor by commands, but by largeness of heart and by giving and bestowing!

9.21.16.en: * When I look around me, I long to love every person without exception.

9.21.17.en: But who can give largeness to my heart except You?

9.21.18.en: I lift the eyes of my heart to Your throne, and I am filled with honor, and I realize Your pride in me, I feel that I am a son among Your sons!

9.21.19.en: You lift me from the dust to heaven.

9.21.20.en: You raise me from weakness to strength, * I confess to You that I am weak, and my days are few and numbered.

9.21.21.en: And my understanding of things is feeble.

9.21.22.en: But there is no place in me for faintheartedness.
